name: Temurah (Substitution of Consecrated Animals)
notes: The act of substituting a non-sacred animal for a consecrated one; both become sacred and the owner receives lashes. Core topic of tractate Temurah.

name: Temurah Taking Effect (Bidieved)
notes: Though substitution is prohibited, once done it takes halakhic effect; both original and substitute become sacred.

name: Temurah: Individual vs. Communal Offerings
notes: Only individual owners can effect substitution; communal offerings and partners cannot render substitutes.

name: Kohen's Ownership of Priestly Gifts and Substitution
hebrew: בעלות כהן על מתנות כהונה לענין תמורה
notes: Dispute between R. Yochanan ben Nuri and R. Akiva whether a kohen who received a firstborn can effect substitution, hinging on when ownership is acquired.

name: Five Sin Offerings Left to Die
notes: Halacha leMoshe miSinai: five categories of sin offerings that are sequestered and left to die — offspring of chatat, substitute of chatat, chatat whose owner died, chatat after owner achieved atonement with another, chatat whose year passed.

name: Offspring of a Sin Offering (Vlad Chatat)
notes: The offspring of a sin offering is left to die and may not be sacrificed or used for benefit.

name: Sin Offering After Owner Achieved Atonement
notes: A sin offering found after its owner achieved atonement with a different animal is left to die. Extensive discussion of cases with money and animals replacing each other.

name: Offspring of Consecrated Animals (Vlad Kodashim)
notes: Status of offspring born to consecrated animals; inherits the sanctity of the parent offering (e.g., offspring of shelamim is shelamim, offspring of olah follows olah rules).

name: Comparative Stringencies: Temurah vs. Kodashim
hebrew: חומרות תמורה על קדשים וקדשים על תמורה
notes: Mishnah 2:3 compares stringencies unique to temurah (e.g., blemished animal gains inherent sanctity, no redemption of wool/labor) vs. those unique to consecrated animals.

name: Unwitting Substitution Treated as Intentional
notes: The Torah treats one who substitutes unintentionally like one who acts intentionally — the substitution takes effect. Contrasted with consecration where unwitting act is ineffective.

name: Animals Disqualified from the Altar (Issurei Mizbeach — Specific Cases)
notes: Tractate Temurah ch. 6 details nine categories of animals prohibited on the altar: copulated with, object of bestiality, set-aside for idolatry, worshipped, payment to prostitute, price of a dog, kilayim, tereifa, yotzei dofen.

name: Payment to Prostitute and Price of Dog — Altar Prohibition
notes: Detailed rules on what constitutes etnan zonah and mechir kelev that disqualify an animal from the altar, including barter, maidservant cases, and whether offspring are also prohibited.

name: Caesarean-Born Animal (Yotzei Dofen) in Kodashim
notes: An animal born by caesarean section is disqualified from the altar and cannot effect temurah.

name: Differences Between Altar Consecrations and Temple Maintenance Consecrations
hebrew: הבדלים בין קדשי מזבח לקדשי בדק הבית
notes: Ch. 7 systematically enumerates distinctions: temurah, piggul/notar/tumah liability, offspring/milk restrictions, slaughter outside courtyard, unspecified consecrations, effect on all items, liability for by-products.

name: Burial of Prohibited Sacred Items (Kevurah)
notes: Items from which benefit is forbidden that must be buried rather than burned: fetus of consecrated animal, placenta, stoned ox, eglah arufah, metzora birds, nazirite's hair, peter chamor, basar bechalav, non-sacred animals slaughtered in courtyard.

name: Burning vs. Burial — Method of Destruction for Prohibited Items
notes: Distinction between items requiring burning (chametz, impure terumah, orlah, kilei hakerem, piggul/notar offerings) and items requiring burial; the two categories cannot be switched even for stringency.

name: Asham Taluy After Determination of Sin
notes: A provisional guilt offering (asham taluy) that is found unnecessary when the person learns he did not sin — it is burned, per R. Yehuda buried.

name: Firstborn and Animal Tithe Offerings from Outside Eretz Yisrael
notes: Firstborn and animal tithe should not be brought to the Temple from outside Eretz Yisrael ab initio; if brought unblemished they are sacrificed, if blemished eaten in place.

name: Eating Rules for Firstborn and Animal Tithe (vs. Other Kodashim)
hebrew: דיני אכילת בכור ומעשר לעומת שאר קדשים
notes: Firstborn and tithe differ from other kodashim: not sold in market by litra, not subject to redemption, sold/eaten only from home; their substitutes and offspring graze until blemished then eaten.

name: Designating a Fetus in the Womb as an Offering
notes: One can preemptively designate the fetus in the womb as a burnt or peace offering before birth, thereby avoiding the firstborn obligation. Rules for twins, tumtum, hermaphrodite.

name: Female Animal Designated for a Male-Only Offering
notes: If one designated a female for a burnt offering or guilt offering (which require males), the animal grazes until blemished, is sold, and the proceeds fund the proper offering.

name: Substitution for Limbs and Fetuses
notes: One cannot substitute for consecrated limbs or fetuses with whole animals, nor whole animals for limbs; dispute of R. Yosei whether substituting a limb consecrates the entire animal.

name: Simultaneous Designation of One Animal for Two Offerings
notes: Dispute (R. Meir vs. R. Yosei) about what happens when one simultaneously or sequentially designates an animal as substitute for both a burnt offering and a peace offering.

name: Formulas That Effect Temurah
notes: Which verbal formulas effect temurah: 'in place of,' 'substitute,' 'exchange for' — effective; 'desacralized' — not temurah, but if blemished animal, effects redemption.

name: Set-Aside and Worshipped Animals — Prohibited for Altar
notes: Animal set aside for idol worship (muktzeh) vs. animal actually worshipped (ne'evad) — both prohibited on altar; distinction regarding what is on them and their consumption.

name: Offspring of a Tereifa Animal and Altar Eligibility
notes: Dispute whether offspring of a tereifa may be sacrificed on the altar (R. Eliezer prohibits, Rabbis permit). Also R. Chanina: animal that suckled from a tereifa is disqualified.

name: Prohibited Animals Mixed with Permitted — Altar Nullification Rules
notes: Animals prohibited on the altar (the nine categories) prohibit an entire mixture in any amount — no nullification applies, unlike food mixtures.

name: Differences Between Individual and Communal Offerings
hebrew: הבדלים בין קרבנות יחיד לקרבנות ציבור
notes: Systematic list: individual offerings — temurah, male or female, require compensation; communal offerings — override Shabbat and tumah, fixed time determines this rule per R. Meir.
